div.head: V As 1.5
div.ab: ⁊ nemne man on ælces gerefan manunge swa fela manna swa man wite, þæt ungelygne syn, þæt hy beon to gewitnesse gehwylcere spræce. ⁊ sien heora aþas ungelygenra manna be þæs feos wyrðe butan cyre.
And nemne mon ylces gerefan monunge swa feala manna swa mon wite, þæt ungelegene syn, þæt beon to gewitnesse gehwylcre spræce. And syn heora aþas ungelægenra manna be ðæs feos wyrþe butan cyre.

Et nominentur in manunga singulorum prepositorum tot homines quot pernoscuntur esse credibiles, qui sint in testimonio singularum causarum. Et sint eorum iuramenta credibilium hominum secundum precium earum butan cyre (id est sine eleccione).
⁊ nemne man on ælces gerefan manunge swa fela manna swa man wite, þæt ungelygne syn, þæt hy beon to gewitnesse gehwylcere spræce. ⁊ sien heora aþas ungelygenra manna be þæs feos wyrðe butan cyre.

Und im Gerichtsbezirk jedes Vogts ernenne man so viele Männer, wie man als wahrhaft kennt, dass sie jedem Rechtsfalle als Zeugen dienen. Und es gelten ihre Eide als die von wahrhaften Männern, je nach dem Sachwerth [des Eingeklagten steige ihre Zahl] ohne Auswahl [durch den Gegner].

And in every reeve's district let as many men be named as are known to be truthful, that they may serve as witnesses in every suit. And let their oaths count as those of truthful men, [their number rising] according to the value of the property [claimed], without selection [by the opponent].

And in every reeve’s district, as many men as are known to be honest shall be nominated to be witnesses in all suits. And the number of honest men required to give oaths [in each case] shall be in proportion to the value of the [disputed] goods, and they shall be ‘unselected.'

And in the district of every reeve as many men are to be nominated as are known to be trustworthy, that they may be witnesses in every suit; the oaths of them, the trustworthy men, are to be in proportion to the value of the property [in dispute], without selection.

Diesen Satz und V 2 mit Schmid S. xlvi, weil ihr Inhalt früher und später vorkommt, anzuzweifeln, seh ich keinen Grund
I see no reason to doubt this sentence and V 2, with Schmid p. xlvi, because their content occurs earlier and later
Q übs. dies Wort (Amtssprengel, wo die Vorladung [s. d. Gl 1] gilt) anderswo durch mannitio, das er auch fürs synonyme folgoð verwendet
Elsewhere Q translates this word (the official district within which the summons [see that word in Gl 1] is valid) by mannitio, which he also uses for the synonymous folgoð
Das Gericht, nicht der Vogt (s. d. Gl 2 e) allein, unter dem ich nicht bloss einen Sheriff verstehe
The court, not the reeve (see that word in Gl 2 e) alone, by whom I do not understand merely a sheriff

Entweder meint As die Geschäftszeugen (s. Gl Kaufzeugen 7 b), die ebenfalls ständig und vom Gericht ernannt bald nach ihm vorkommen, oder den schon unter II Ew 2 bestehenden Ausschuss des Gerichts; s. d. Gl 20 a—c

As means either the witnesses to transactions (see Gl Kaufzeugen 7 b), who, likewise permanent and appointed by the court, appear soon after him, or the committee of the court already existing under II Ew 2; see that word in Gl 20 a—c

Zunächst bei Handel und den daraus entstehenden Streitsachen, dann als Zeugen des ja nicht schriftlichen Urteils, drittens als Eidhelfer, was ja gewitnes und testis auch heissen kann und laut des Satzendes u.⁷ hier mitbedeuten muss

In the first place in trading and the disputes arising from it, secondly as witnesses to the judgment, which of course was not written, thirdly as oath-helpers, which gewitnes and testis can of course also mean, and which, according to the end of the sentence below⁷, they must also mean here
Nur só viele aus dieser Kommission brauchen mitzuschwören, dass die Summe ihrer Eideswerte den Klageeidwert erreicht
Only so many members of this commission need to swear with him that the sum of their oath-values reaches the value of the oath of accusation
Gegner oder Richter hat nicht das Recht, zur Erschwerung des Eides die Mitschwörer zu bestimmen; s. Gl Auswahleid 1. 5
Neither the opponent nor the judge has the right to designate the co-swearers so as to make the oath harder; see Gl Auswahleid 1. 5

According to Liebermann a fresh nomination of witnesses would not be made in each new case. The persons specified were a permanent body who served as co-swearers as well as witnesses (cf. II Edw. cap. 2; IV Edg. cap. 3, 4, 5).
Cf. I Edw. cap. 1 § 3, note 1.
